craft_evidence.owned: claim+press: brand history says a new factory was built in Middleborough MA in 1970 "where production continues today"; footer 1 Taunton St, Middleborough; NYT 2011 (via Wikipedia) ~100 workers there. No factory-tour page read.
craft_evidence.makers: brand is its own maker (single Middleborough factory per brand history); no third-party maker named; SF shop feed vendor field = "Alden Shoe Company"
craft_evidence.mills: not on brand pages: aldenshoe.com shell cordovan page says only "the single tannery still producing genuine shell cordovan" (unnamed). Horween named by The Alden Shop SF collection handle (horween-shell-cordovan) and by Horween/Chicago Tribune via Wikipedia (supplier since c.1930) - third-party evid
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed (brand history page): founded 1884 by Charles H. Alden, Middleborough MA; moved to Brockton 1933; new Middleborough factory 1970; "still family owned"
craft_evidence.process: partial: Genuine Welt Construction page explains why welting (renewable sole attachment, lateral stability); Genuine Shell Cordovan page states pure vegetable tannage, hand finishing, six-month tannag
craft_evidence.reasoning: Alden states it makes its shoes in its own Middleborough, MA factory (built 1970, company founded 1884 in the same town), so the maker and the brand are the same thing; NYT 2011 corroborates the factory and workforce. Process pages explain Goodyear welting and six-month vegetable-tanned shell cordovan, but the brand site names no tannery (Horween is named only by third parties and the SF shop) and does not state made-in on a readable product page, so the 5 rests on the owned factory, not on documented supply.

ownership.owner: private, family-owned (brand history: "still family owned"); no filings
